Published online:
    August 31, 2026

Geographic focus:
    United States (primary); Japan, Eurozone, Gulf region (secondary)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Friday remarks have sharply repriced September rate hike odds from ~35% to 64%. Markets now pivot to August payrolls (Friday, +55K consensus) and upcoming CPI/PPI prints (Sept 10-11) as the key gatekeepers for a Sept 15-16 Fed decision. The dollar index pulled back slightly from two-week highs but remains firm, pressuring the yen past 160 before a modest recovery on Bessent's BoJ comments. Euro and sterling held monthly gains. Oil bid on Gulf tensions.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (the article centers on Fed rate hike expectations, dollar dynamics driven by Warsh's hawkish pivot, and upcoming US macro data)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 85 (strongly oriented toward a rate hike scenario)
Probability of increase: 64% (directly cited fed funds futures pricing)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 20 (holding is implicitly the alternative if payrolls disappoint, but not the article's thrust)
Probability of holding: 36% (residual probability implied by futures pricing)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (cuts are not discussed or implied anywhere in the article)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 70 (meaningfully more hawkish than before — Warsh's deliberate signaling, the sharp repricing from 35% to 64% hike odds, and the upcoming inflation prints all tilt the near-term rate path higher; the only offset is downside payroll risk which could block the hike)
